text:
You need to turn report data from Excel sheets into an HTML design that is clear, clean, and easy to use.

I’m Mina Castellan, and I have 5 years of experience in data analysis, dashboard building, data cleaning, and data visualization using SQL, Excel, Power BI, and Google Sheets. For this kind of work, I focus on organizing the source data properly first, then shaping it into a polished report structure that is easy to read in HTML.

One relevant project I built was the Sales KPI dashboard for Marlowe Furniture in retail. I created one Power BI report on a star-schema model to replace 14 separate Excel sales reports. That work also reduced the monthly close reporting process from 3 days to 4 hours. While the tools and end format were different, the core challenge was the same: taking Excel-based reporting data and turning it into a cleaner, more useful reporting experience.

For your project, I can help review the Excel sheets, identify the report structure, and translate the data into a design that supports the content well. I’m comfortable working with structured data, cleaning inconsistencies, and making sure the final presentation is organized and visually readable. If needed, I can also help think through how the report should be grouped and displayed so the HTML output matches the intent of the Excel source.

My background with dashboards has taught me how important layout, hierarchy, and clarity are when raw data needs to become a report that people can actually use. I’m careful with details, and I like making sure the final output is both accurate and presentable.

If you’d like, I can start by reviewing the Excel sheets and outlining the report structure before the HTML design is built. What is the expected layout for the final HTML report?
